headline: Breach at Belfast-based supplier affects dozens of Irish credit unions and went unnoticed for six weeks
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission says it has received more than 40 breach notifications from credit unions. They used a Belfast-based company as a data processor, and that company suffered a breach. The breach reportedly went undetected for about six weeks.

headline: Data of thousands of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase customers reported stolen
summary: Attackers reportedly stole data belonging to thousands of customers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase. The source summary is cut off and does not give further details.

headline: JPMorgan confirms customer data breach tied to third party; N0n claims Visa and Mastercard leaks
summary: JPMorgan has confirmed that customer data was exposed after a third party was compromised. The ransomware actor N0n claims attacks on JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard and reportedly leaked customer data. The scope and the third party's identity are not stated.

headline: N-able says server breach caused a worldwide outage of Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud services
summary: N-able says attackers breached one of its servers and caused a major worldwide outage of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email filtering services. The source does not say what the attackers accessed beyond the outage itself.

headline: European Commission confirms cyberattack; CERT-EU reportedly links it to ARTEX AI hacking platform
summary: The European Commission has confirmed it suffered a cyberattack. Citing earlier POLITICO reporting, The Record says CERT-EU found the attackers used ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform. The FBI recently warned that both criminals and state-sponsored groups use ARTEX. The source does not describe the scope of the attack or who carried it out.

headline: Metasploit adds exploits for exploited Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaws, BeyondTrust RS and Zimbra
summary: The latest Metasploit release adds public exploit modules for two Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated RCE flaws, CVE-2026-76519 and CVE-2026-76461, both reportedly exploited in the wild. It also adds an unauthenticated RCE module for BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764). Further modules cover Zimbra impersonation and rate-limit bypass flaws (CVE-2026-73571, CVE-2026-93637) and an Openfire bypass (CVE-2024-25420).

headline: European Commission confirms cyberattack using public AI tool forced applications offline
summary: The European Commission confirmed it was hit by a cyberattack that misused a publicly available AI tool. Several applications were taken offline. Details on the affected systems and whether staff data was exposed were not clear from the briefing.

headline: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack that disrupted services
summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack it describes as AI-assisted, which led it to take some services offline for containment. The Commission says it has no evidence of a data breach.

headline: European Commission confirms reportedly AI-driven cyberattack took some systems offline
summary: The European Commission has confirmed a cyberattack that targeted "individual systems" and took some of them offline. According to reports, the attackers used a tool called ARTEX, but the details have not been confirmed.

headline: Second Norwegian energy company breached within two days
summary: A second Norwegian energy company has reported a breach, two days after a similar incident at another firm. No link between the two has been established, although they appear similar.

headline: F5 patches five critical NGINX vulnerabilities enabling possible remote code execution
summary: F5 fixed five critical NGINX flaws, collectively dubbed "NGINX2Root", that may allow remote code execution under certain conditions. Several research teams independently reported two of them. No in-the-wild exploitation or KEV listing has been reported.

summary: The PHP Foundation has released security updates for several critical flaws, including CVE-2026-115560. Some of the flaws could allow remote code execution. The US Department of Justice has assessed that the group operates within Russia's FSB. Its targets are government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America.

summary: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) in Cisco Expressway shortly after a public proof-of-concept appeared. headline: Transport for London breach may have exposed data of 265,000 Oyster photocard users
summary: Transport for London says account details of about 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have been exposed in a data breach. The source gives no detail on how the breach happened.

headline: N-able attributes Mail Assure and SpamExperts service disruption to a cyberattack
summary: N-able says a cyberattack caused the disruption to its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email security services. The company indicated the incident could have led to credential theft. MSPs and their customers use these services, which creates potential downstream exposure.

headline: SonicWall ends security patches for Gen 6 firewalls and urges immediate replacement
summary: SonicWall says Generation 6 firewalls will no longer get security patches, including for critical flaws. It tells customers to replace them and remove them from the internet edge. The vendor expects attackers using automation and AI to target exposed unsupported devices, but this is a forecast, not observed exploitation.

headline: Linux KVM flaw CVE-2026-99312 lets guest VMs read host memory on AMD hosts with nested virtualization
summary: A Linux KVM flaw, CVE-2026-99312, allowed researchers to read about 127 GB of host memory from their own guest VM on DigitalOcean. On shared servers, that memory can include other tenants' VMs. The flaw affects only AMD hosts with nested virtualization enabled, and fixed kernels have shipped. The source reports no in-the-wild exploitation.

headline: Ruby patches heap overflow CVE-2026-132825 ('Ruby2Shell') with possible RCE
summary: SecurityWeek: The Ruby maintainers fixed CVE-2026-132825, a heap-based buffer overflow they call Ruby2Shell. It could lead to remote code execution. The source does not report any exploitation. Amazon Linux Security Center: Ruby versions before 3.3.14, 3.4.13 and 4.0.10 can write one byte past a heap buffer during case conversion, for example with the ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252 encodings. No exploitation or severity score is reported, and Amazon Linux status is not stated.

headline: Transport for London breach may have exposed data of 265,000 Oyster photocard holders
summary: TfL warned that account details of about 265,000 Oyster photocard holders may have been compromised, including children with Zip cards and holders of the 60+ card. TfL detected suspicious activity on the photocard website on 16 November and took the system offline.

headline: Drupal patches critical core installer flaw enabling unauthenticated site takeover in uncommon setups
summary: Drupal released fixes for all supported branches to address a critical core flaw. Under specific conditions, an unauthenticated attacker could use the built-in installer to try to reinstall a site, which could lead to site takeover or remote code execution. The project says the vulnerable configurations are uncommon, and the source does not report any exploitation.

headline: Compromised third-party web script served malicious JavaScript to visitors of major brand websites
summary: Qualys describes a recent supply-chain incident in which a widely used third-party web service delivered malicious JavaScript to visitors of sites run by news publishers, banks, airlines and software firms. Most affected organizations did not deploy the bad code themselves. They received it through a script they had chosen to trust. The source does not name the service or say how long the exposure lasted.

headline: ASUS patches critical hard-coded key flaws in Control Center Express
summary: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to fix three critical vulnerabilities, including a hard-coded key flaw. The flaws could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages. The report does not mention any exploitation.

headline: Attacker abuses CyberPower PowerPanel UPS software to run scripts on a domain controller
summary: Symantec reported that an attacker used CyberPower's PowerPanel UPS management software to run malicious scripts on a domain controller. The source does not say how the software was compromised, whether a CVE is involved, or how widespread the activity is.

headline: SBC Medical Group discloses breaches exposing data of 1.6 million people
summary: SBC Medical Group disclosed two cybersecurity incidents in a filing with the US SEC. Sensitive customer and employee information was exposed, including personal data belonging to 1.6 million people.

headline: PHP SOAP extension use-after-free lets unauthenticated requests crash PHP processes (CVE-2026-129506)
summary: PHP's SOAP extension can read freed memory when parsing XML that has a DTD and an entity reference inside an attribute value. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach an exposed SOAP endpoint can crash the PHP process. Applications that load attacker-controlled WSDL or schema documents may also be affected. The record does not report exploitation, and it does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

Data leaks only if the application exposes the decoded array; fixed in 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13.

summary: The Dutch municipality of Dordrecht processed sensitive personal data about its residents unlawfully for several years. The report describes this as a long-running privacy violation.

headline: PHP 8.6 released with stricter default session security settings
summary: PHP 8.6 adds new language features and turns on safer session defaults: strict mode, HttpOnly cookies and SameSite=Lax. Custom session handlers that lack create_sid() and validateId() are now deprecated. Apps that relied on the old defaults should test their login flows.

headline: UK government carried out a covert operation to secure refrigeration systems at supermarkets and warehouses
summary: The source reports that the UK government ran a large-scale secret operation to secure refrigeration systems at supermarkets, warehouses and other sites. The available summary gives no details about the threat or the systems involved.

headline: Git LFS flaw CVE-2026-105802 lets malicious repositories execute commands; fixed in 3.8.1
summary: Git LFS versions 0.6.0 through 3.8.0 do not check submodule configuration values for embedded control characters. A malicious repository could use this to run an attacker-controlled command while objects are fetched or added. Version 3.8.1 fixes the flaw; no exploitation has been reported.

headline: Git LFS .lfsconfig filtering flaw allows command execution when fetching objects; fixed in 3.8.1
summary: Git LFS versions 1.3.0 up to but not including 3.8.1 do not properly filter option keys in a repository's .lfsconfig file. A crafted key can set a custom transfer command, which then runs an attacker-chosen command when objects are fetched. Version 3.8.1 fixes the issue; no exploitation has been reported.

headline: Large-scale campaign uses mail bombing followed by fake IT helpdesk calls to take over accounts
summary: Researchers found a large campaign in which attackers first flood users' inboxes with email. They then pose as IT helpdesk staff and use the confusion to gain access to user accounts.

headline: ROMULUS ClickFix delivery platform spreads new RAT resembling CNCMachineRMS
summary: Researchers at Blackpoint report that the ROMULUS ClickFix delivery platform is distributing a previously undocumented remote access trojan with similarities to CNCMachineRMS. ROMULUS appears to work as a delivery service, pushing CNCMachineRMS and Legion Loader through separate chains while relying on ClickFix lures and sideloading via signed binaries.

headline: UK tribunal confirms government served Apple a secret notice targeting iCloud encryption
summary: A UK tribunal has confirmed that the British government served Apple with a secret legal notice aimed at the cryptographic protections on iCloud accounts. The ruling ends nearly two years in which officials refused to acknowledge a notice that had already been widely reported.

headline: DOJ and DHS launch Threat Disruption Center to tackle scams and cybercrime
summary: The US Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security have created a joint Threat Disruption Center. The unit will triage victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks and give private-sector organizations that work with victims a direct channel to the government.

headline: Google to expand Android developer verification to all countries from January 2027
summary: Google will require developer identity verification for apps from every install source on certified Android devices worldwide, starting in January 2027. Unverified apps will lose the normal install experience. The rollout starts with seven app distributors, and the headline says power users will get an alternative route.

headline: Dutch Public Prosecution Service reportedly hacked Tata Steel network during criminal probe
summary: Security.NL reports that the Dutch Public Prosecution Service (Openbaar Ministerie) hacked Tata Steel's corporate network as part of its criminal investigation into the company. The source excerpt does not give details of the method or legal basis. This is a lawful-access matter, not a criminal cyberattack.

headline: Study: retraining AI agents on more prompt-injection attacks can weaken their defenses
summary: Researchers from Waterloo, Zhejiang University and KTH found that AI agents retrained on larger sets of prompt-injection attacks became easier to hijack in three of four tests. The red-teaming tool that found the most working attacks produced the weakest defense, apparently because many of its findings were redundant.

headline: Linux kernel netfilter nft_payload flaw fixed by restricting checksum offsets
summary: A Linux kernel fix for netfilter nft_payload limits checksum offsets to known values. The CVE record gives no severity and no exploitation details, and it does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Microsoft lets antivirus vendors run their security engines outside the Windows kernel
summary: Microsoft now lets antivirus vendors run their scanners outside the Windows kernel. The aim is to lower the risk of catastrophic system crashes caused by faulty security software.
watch_tech: Defender for Endpoint; CrowdStrike Falcon; SentinelOne

headline: Talos links Solana blockchain-based C2 RAT to suspected North Korea-aligned UAT-12643
summary: Cisco Talos has linked a remote access trojan to a group it tracks as UAT-12643, which is suspected of being aligned with North Korea. The RAT hides its command-and-control channel on the Solana blockchain, and the report says it can survive Windows resets. The source does not name targeted sectors or regions.

headline: US charges man allegedly hired by Russia to spy on Silicon Valley tech and defense firm
summary: US federal prosecutors have charged a 25-year-old man with spying on a Silicon Valley technology and defense company on Russia's behalf. He is accused of surveilling employees, including at a coffee shop and in an aggressive car pursuit.

headline: SBC Medical Group breach exposes data of over 2 million customers of Japanese clinics
summary: Attackers accessed databases holding customer information for SBC Medical Group clinics in Japan. More than 2 million people are affected.

headline: CVE-2026-126714: partially overwritten session files may enable remote code execution
summary: A CVE record says partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution. The record does not name the affected product, and Amazon Linux affected status and patch availability are not established. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: Google rolls out Android developer verification requirement worldwide
summary: Google is expanding its verification requirement for Android developers to all regions. The requirement launched in September in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. It is intended to make it harder to distribute malicious apps.

headline: Timezone cache use-after-free flaw may allow remote code execution
summary: A CVE record describes a use-after-free in a timezone cache that could lead to remote code execution. It does not name the affected component, severity or exploitation status. It also does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: UK court orders government to confirm it requested an Apple iCloud backdoor
summary: A British court has ruled that the UK government must confirm it asked Apple for an iCloud backdoor. The decision bears on the debate over encryption and government access powers in the UK.

headline: Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown (CVE-2026-129481)
summary: CVE-2026-129481 is a use-after-free bug that can occur when a session shutdown is interrupted. The record does not name the affected component or give a severity. Amazon Linux has not confirmed whether its packages are affected or whether a patch exists.

headline: Guide to hardening GitHub Actions pipelines against insider threats and stolen credentials
summary: Socket published practical guidance on protecting CI/CD pipelines from misuse of stolen credentials. It covers GitHub Actions configuration, trusted publishing, release approvals and credential revocation.

headline: US lawmakers form bipartisan AI safety caucus
summary: A new congressional AI safety caucus has launched with 26 founding members, seven of them Republicans. It forms amid rising security concerns about AI. The White House continues to oppose AI regulation.

headline: Postman survey: AI agents call production APIs, but credential governance is lagging
summary: A Postman survey of nearly 9,000 developers, architects and executives found that a quarter of organizations already have AI agents calling their APIs in production. About four in ten respondents have not settled how agents should handle credentials and identity.

headline: CISA nominee LoSapio pledges stronger cyber defenses at Senate confirmation hearing
summary: Michael LoSapio, the administration's nominee to lead CISA, told lawmakers he would look for gaps within the agency. During the hearing he also disputed that the Capitol was attacked on January 6, 2021.

headline: Democrats call CISA nominee LoSapio 'disqualified' after contentious hearing
summary: Michael LoSapio is a Palantir executive and the administration's nominee for CISA. At his hearing he clashed with Democratic committee members over the 2020 election and January 6. Democrats afterwards called him disqualified.

headline: Sean Cairncross leaves post as US National Cyber Director
summary: Sean Cairncross is out as US National Cyber Director. During his tenure he was involved in administration decisions on AI security and critical infrastructure protection. The source summary does not give the reasons or name a successor.

headline: House hearing examines outage risks and AI-driven vulnerability discovery in aging US infrastructure
summary: Reporting on a US House hearing says that as AI finds more serious software flaws, businesses will struggle to upgrade aging systems. The piece is commentary on future risk, not a report of a specific incident.

headline: Qwen incidents highlight need for stronger control of self-hosted AI agents
summary: An opinion piece argues that companies running self-hosted AI agents may overestimate how much control they have. It cites several Qwen-related incidents as evidence that businesses need ways to enforce directions on model behaviour. The source summary gives no technical details.

headline: CISO survey points to growing comfort with autonomous AI agents in SOC operations
summary: An a16z survey of CISOs at large organisations found that 36% are comfortable today letting AI agents act on their own for low-risk security actions. That figure is expected to reach 60% within 12 months, and AI SOC ranked as the top initiative for 2027. The piece is a commentary and trend article, not a report of a threat.

headline: Vendor article outlines early warning signs of ransomware intrusions before encryption
summary: An Acronis-sponsored article describes five early signs that a ransomware intrusion is under way, including credential theft, lateral movement and attempts to disable security tools. It is general detection guidance and does not cover a specific incident.

headline: CISA director nominee avoids budget and staffing questions at confirmation hearing
summary: Michael LoSapio, a Palantir executive nominated to lead CISA, avoided questions on the agency's budget, staffing and priorities at his confirmation hearing. The outcome remains uncertain.

headline: Dutch data protection authority fines company On That Ass €90,000 for GDPR breach
summary: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) has fined the company On That Ass €90,000 for breaking the GDPR. The source summary does not give details of the violation.

headline: Opinion: retire vanity security dashboards and fix recurring IT/OT alert noise
summary: An OT security architect argues in a video that security teams should drop vanity dashboard metrics. His example is a manufacturing site where approved maintenance work triggers the same alert every week. He recommends that SOC and control-engineering teams review these patterns together and tune detections.

headline: Linux kernel rxrpc fix for tx_pending update made without holding a lock (CVE-2026-99350)
summary: A Linux kernel fix corrects rxrpc code that updated call->tx_pending without holding the required lock. The record gives no impact or exploitation details, and Amazon Linux status is not established.

headline: Survey: few organizations can reach critical network gear quickly during outages or attacks
summary: An Opengear survey of 514 CIOs and CISOs found that only a small share could get secure management access to critical network infrastructure immediately once the primary network fails. This gap matters most when teams need to isolate systems and restore services during ransomware attacks or after faulty updates.

headline: Signal to shield chats from Apple and Google AI agents
summary: Signal plans protections to keep users' chats away from operating-system AI agents from Apple and Google. It warns that this alone is not enough.

headline: Dutch consumer association criticises banks for pushing customers onto mobile apps
summary: The Consumentenbond, the Dutch consumers' association, says banks increasingly push customers into using their banking apps. It wants full alternatives for banking without a smartphone.

headline: Industry experts discuss recent major outages and the role of AI-accelerated patching
summary: SecurityWeek collected expert comments on recent major outages, including whether AI-accelerated patching played a part. The commentary stresses tested rollback plans and the fragility of interconnected systems.

headline: AI product founder reports widespread token fraud through free-trial abuse
summary: The founder of ChatPRD describes groups abusing free trials and promo codes to get AI usage, resell tokens or run their own businesses on top of the product's agent. She is ending free trials in response. The blogger who shared the video suggests the abusers' prompts were partly used to work out which model was underneath.

headline: Dutch data protection authority publishes template text for banning camera glasses
summary: The Dutch data protection authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) has published standard wording that organisations can use in their house rules to ban camera glasses. It is privacy guidance aimed at organisations in the Netherlands.

headline: Rubrik report puts median ransomware recovery time at 20 days
summary: A Rubrik report finds that ransomware victims take a median of 20 days to recover. It says 28% of recovery cases take more than six weeks.

headline: Linux kernel HID mcp2221 driver fix for init_work initialization and cancellation (CVE-2026-99329)
summary: A Linux kernel flaw in the HID mcp2221 driver has been fixed. The fix makes sure the driver's init_work is always initialized and cancelled. The Amazon Linux record does not say which distribution builds are affected, what the severity is, or whether a patch is available.

headline: Use-after-free tied to last_fatal_error_backtrace global being repopulated after shutdown
summary: A use-after-free can occur when the last_fatal_error_backtrace global is filled in again after shutdown. The record does not name the affected product or give a severity, and it does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Video discussion examines alert fatigue and panic over high-severity flaws in the AI era
summary: A Dark Reading video segment looks at how recent high-severity vulnerability disclosures, together with fears of AI-assisted exploitation, have caused panic, operational disruption and warning fatigue. It is commentary and contains no new technical findings.

headline: Weekly roundup: AI jailbreak flaws, PNG-based malware loader and large ransom demands
summary: This weekly recap covers about twenty items, including reported jailbreak flaws in an AI model, a malware loader that uses PNG files, and large ransom demands. Its theme is attackers abusing familiar lures such as job offers and outage notices. The excerpt gives few specifics.

headline: Censys blog says AI SOC effectiveness depends on its context layer
summary: A Censys blog post argues that an AI-driven SOC depends more on the context its agents can reach than on the model itself. It covers tasks such as alert summarisation, enrichment and drafting detections.

headline: Calendar sharing permission flaw lets mayWriteOwn sharees edit or delete any event
summary: A user with mayWriteOwn access to another user's calendar could change or delete any event in it, not only the events they organised. The record does not name the affected product or give a severity, and it does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Cyrus IMAP 3.12.5 release fixes an unspecified security issue
summary: A CVE record points to the security fixes in the Cyrus IMAP 3.12.5 release notes. The record gives no details of the flaw or its impact, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: Linux kernel KVM TDX fix enables Bus Lock VM exit
summary: A Linux kernel fix turns on the Bus Lock VM exit for KVM TDX guests. The record gives no impact details, and it does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Linux kernel KVM x86/xen fix enforces vcpu_info registration alignment
summary: A Linux kernel fix makes KVM's Xen emulation require 4-byte alignment when vcpu_info is registered. The record gives no impact or severity details, and it does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Linux kernel KVM PPC Book3S HV fix adds preemption protection around HPTE bit-lock users
summary: A Linux kernel flaw in KVM on PowerPC Book3S HV has been fixed. The fix disables preemption around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users. The record does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched, gives no severity, and reports no exploitation.

headline: libFLAC relative symlink handling flaw can overwrite files during metadata edits
summary: A flaw in libFLAC lets a size-changing metadata edit on a FLAC file that is a relative symlink write to a path resolved against the process working directory. An attacker who plants such a symlink can cause a victim's edit to overwrite files. The record does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: PostgreSQL 19 released after delay attributed to a surge of AI-reported vulnerabilities
summary: PostgreSQL 19 shipped two months later than usual. The delay is attributed to the volume of AI-reported vulnerability issues the team had to handle. A new WAIT FOR LSN command lets applications read their own writes on standby servers.

headline: Microsoft begins automatic Windows 11 26H2 upgrades on unmanaged devices
summary: Microsoft has started automatically upgrading eligible personal and unmanaged PCs to Windows 11 26H2. Devices managed by IT departments are not covered by this rollout.

headline: Microsoft releases Windows 11 KB5132057 November preview update with 28 changes
summary: Microsoft has released the optional KB5132057 preview update for Windows 11. It includes 28 changes and fixes, including improvements to Windows Search, Windows Hello and the Run dialog. The source does not mention any security fixes.

headline: Talos opinion piece urges environment awareness and team stability over reactive patching
summary: A Cisco Talos newsletter column argues that security teams should prioritize understanding their environment and keeping teams stable rather than constantly reacting to patch news. It reports no new threat.

headline: Linux kernel fixes deadlock in Lenovo Go S HID driver when a device is removed during setup (CVE-2026-99326)
summary: A fix in the Linux kernel's hid-lenovo-go-s driver prevents a deadlock that can happen if the device is removed during setup. The flaw requires local hardware and affects a niche handheld-device driver.

headline: Linux kernel hid-lenovo-go-s driver fix adds suspend handling and gated access
summary: A Linux kernel fix to the Lenovo Legion Go S HID driver adds a suspend function and gates access behind a flag. Only that specific hardware driver is affected.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast podcast for November 17, 2026
summary: SANS ISC published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no content details.

headline: Researchers use CT scanning to open a 400-year-old cryptex padlock
summary: Researchers used CT scanning to recover the code of a centuries-old cryptex padlock and open it. This is a historical curiosity with no enterprise security impact.
